newsitem.title: CHINA: China futures exchange becomes independent.
newsitem.headline: China futures exchange becomes independent.

text.p: China's Chongqing Commodities Exchange has become an independent futures market by setting up a membership system, an exchange statement said on Tuesday.
The exchange, set up in April 1993, was formerly a semi-official exchange jointly run by the local government and government departments.
The statement said the move aimed to strengthen the exchange's self-discipline and supervision of trading through market means.
China has 15 futures exchanges, most of them run by local governments and government departments.
In a recent reform, Beijing ordered all the exchanges to transform themselves into independent entities managed by members who bear the profits and losses themselves.
A few exchanges have already done this, including the Shanghai Commodity Exchange and the Shanghai Metal Exchange.
